title: Semi-Supervised Classification with Graph Convolutional Networks
general_question: Which approach to semi-supervised learning on graph-structured data uses a variant of convolutional neural networks that operates directly on graphs, is motivated by a first-order approximation of spectral graph convolutions, and scales linearly in the number of graph edges?

title: SQuAD: 100,000+ Questions for Machine Comprehension of Text
general_question: Which reading comprehension dataset has more than 100,000 questions posed by crowdworkers on Wikipedia articles, where each answer is a segment of text from the reading passage, and where a logistic regression model reaches 51.0% F1 against 86.8% human performance?

title: Attention Is All You Need
general_question: Which network architecture for sequence transduction is based solely on attention mechanisms, dispensing with recurrence and convolutions entirely, and achieved 28.4 BLEU on the WMT 2014 English-to-German translation task?

title: Proximal Policy Optimization Algorithms
general_question: Which family of policy gradient methods optimizes a surrogate objective with multiple epochs of minibatch updates per data sample, keeps some of the benefits of trust region policy optimization while being much simpler to implement, and was tested on simulated robotic locomotion and Atari game playing?

title: BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding
general_question: Which language representation model pre-trains deep bidirectional representations from unlabeled text by conditioning on both left and right context in all layers, can be fine-tuned with just one additional output layer, and set new state-of-the-art results on eleven NLP tasks including a GLUE score of 80.5%?

title: Deep contextualized word representations
general_question: Which contextualized word representations are learned functions of the internal states of a deep bidirectional language model pre-trained on a large text corpus, model polysemy, and improved the state of the art on six NLP problems when added to existing models?

title: Sentence-BERT: Sentence Embeddings using Siamese BERT-Networks
general_question: Which modification of the pretrained BERT network uses siamese and triplet network structures to derive sentence embeddings that can be compared with cosine similarity, reducing the time to find the most similar pair among 10,000 sentences from about 65 hours to about 5 seconds?

title: RoBERTa: A Robustly Optimized BERT Pretraining Approach
general_question: Which replication study of BERT pretraining measured the impact of key hyperparameters and training data size, found that BERT was significantly undertrained, and achieved state-of-the-art results on GLUE, RACE and SQuAD?

title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks
general_question: Which models combine a pre-trained seq2seq model as parametric memory with a dense vector index of Wikipedia as non-parametric memory, accessed with a pre-trained neural retriever, and compare conditioning on the same retrieved passages for the whole generated sequence with using different passages per token?

title: Dense Passage Retrieval for Open-Domain Question Answering
general_question: Which work shows that passage retrieval for open-domain question answering can be implemented with dense representations alone, learned from a small number of questions and passages by a simple dual-encoder framework, outperforming a Lucene-BM25 system by 9% to 19% absolute in top-20 passage retrieval accuracy?

title: LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models
general_question: Which adaptation method freezes the pre-trained model weights and injects trainable rank decomposition matrices into each layer of the Transformer, reducing the number of trainable parameters by 10,000 times and GPU memory by 3 times compared with fine-tuning GPT-3 175B, with no additional inference latency?

title: Word Alignment by Fine-tuning Embeddings on Parallel Corpora
general_question: Which word alignment method fine-tunes pre-trained multilingual language models on parallel text with objectives designed to improve alignment quality, outperforms previous state-of-the-art models on five language pairs, and is released as an aligner called AWESOME?

title: Chain-of-Thought Prompting Elicits Reasoning in Large Language Models
general_question: Which prompting method provides a large language model with a few demonstrations containing a series of intermediate reasoning steps, improves arithmetic, commonsense and symbolic reasoning, and reaches state-of-the-art accuracy on the GSM8K math word problem benchmark with eight exemplars on a 540B-parameter model?

title: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models
general_question: Which approach uses LLMs to generate reasoning traces and task-specific actions in an interleaved manner, interacts with a simple Wikipedia API on HotpotQA and Fever, and outperforms imitation and reinforcement learning methods on ALFWorld and WebShop by 34% and 10% absolute success rate?

title: RAGAS: Automated Evaluation of Retrieval Augmented Generation
general_question: Which framework puts forward a suite of metrics for reference-free evaluation of retrieval augmented generation pipelines, covering the retrieval of relevant and focused context passages, the faithful use of those passages by the LLM, and the quality of the generation, without relying on ground truth human annotations?

title: Direct Preference Optimization: Your Language Model is Secretly a Reward Model
general_question: Which algorithm introduces a new parameterization of the reward model in RLHF that allows the optimal policy to be extracted in closed form, solving the standard RLHF problem with only a simple classification loss and without sampling from the language model during fine-tuning?

title: Evaluation of Retrieval-Augmented Generation: A Survey
general_question: Which survey of the evaluation and benchmarks of RAG systems conducts a unified evaluation process called Auepora, compares metrics of the retrieval and generation components such as relevance, accuracy and faithfulness, and discusses the limitations of current RAG benchmarks?

title: M3-Embedding: Multi-Linguality, Multi-Functionality, Multi-Granularity Text Embeddings Through Self-Knowledge Distillation
general_question: Which embedding model supports semantic retrieval in more than 100 languages, performs dense, multi-vector and sparse retrieval simultaneously, processes inputs of up to 8,192 tokens, and is trained with a self-knowledge distillation approach that uses the relevance scores of the different retrieval functionalities as the teacher signal?

title: Can LLMs Be Trusted for Evaluating RAG Systems? A Survey of Methods and Datasets
general_question: Which study systematically reviews 63 academic articles on RAG evaluation, focusing on datasets, retrievers, indexing and databases, and the generator component, and observes that an LLM can both generate evaluation datasets and conduct the evaluations for each component?

title: Qwen3 Embedding: Advancing Text Embedding and Reranking Through Foundation Models
general_question: Which series of text embedding and reranking models, the successor of the GTE-Qwen series, is offered in 0.6B, 4B and 8B sizes, uses its backbone LLMs to synthesize training data in a multi-stage training pipeline, and is publicly available under the Apache 2.0 license?

title: Parallel Context-of-Experts Decoding for Retrieval Augmented Generation
general_question: Which training-free framework for retrieval augmented generation treats retrieved documents as isolated experts and synchronizes their predictions with a retrieval-aware contrastive decoding rule that weighs expert logits against the model prior, recovering cross-document reasoning without a shared attention across documents?

title: How Retrieved Context Shapes Internal Representations in RAG
general_question: Which study analyzes how different types of retrieved documents affect the hidden states of LLMs in RAG, and how these internal representation shifts relate to generation behavior, across four question-answering datasets and three LLMs in single- and multi-document settings?
